headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and output-driven errors plausible; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, while plano reads config.yaml and has broad network egress. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other, especially if files or MCP outputs are shared. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through a shared file or MCP tool output
IF Semantic Kernel parses plano-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP tools for the shared workflow
Keep plano outputs in a read-only, non-executable folder
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in prompts
Require provenance tags before any file content is interpreted as instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials. If they share application-defined files or context, sensitive traces, logs, or secrets can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF the two agents share any workspace or memory store containing logs, traces, or credentials
IF Semantic Kernel forwards shared context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Redact logs and traces before handoff
Disable outbound tools for sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed plugin or model keys immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: plano cannot write files or modify git state, but Semantic Kernel can write the filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via memory store. Overlap on mutable application files or shared memory can still cause write conflicts and stale state, even without git. Because only one side has write capability, medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined files
IF multiple Semantic Kernel instances share the same memory store without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Turn on per-run file locking
Use unique memory-store namespaces per instance
Serialize writes through one orchestrator process

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed for function calling against plugins, so it may treat plano outputs as authoritative if the orchestrator wires them together. plano can emit routing or policy text, and Semantic Kernel can act on it through plugins or MCP servers. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so output-to-action cascades are plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes plano output as plugin input without validation
IF downstream plugins execute actions based on plano-generated recommendations
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action tool call
Require schema validation on plano outputs
Log and review all tool-triggering decisions
Restrict action plugins to allowlisted commands

E_compliance.rationale: plano touches logs, traces, and metrics, while Semantic Kernel handles application context plus model provider API keys and plugin credentials. If the pair is used on regulated or residency-bound data, the broader egress and credential handling can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into logs, traces, or application context
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced by the shared workflow
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared prompts
Set explicit retention limits for logs and traces
Use region-pinned model endpoints
Document a data-processing agreement for any cross-service flow
